title: How John Rush builds and grows $5K/month online directories with keyword research, no-code and SEO
summary: John Rush walks through his directory playbook live: validate ideas with Google Keyword Planner, buy a keyword-matching domain, launch a minimal no-code site in one evening, promote on Reddit and social, then add SEO. He also covers monetization (sponsors, affiliates, paid listings), selling directories, and using directories as a traffic channel for SaaS.

principles.text: Start every directory idea with keyword research: check search volume before building anything.
principles.quote: I basically spend hours in that tool every day just throwing all random ideas into that tool and seeing whether there is traffic or not

principles.text: Do the minimum to validate assumptions, then invest real human time only in what wins.
principles.quote: you have to be doing as little as possible to validate all the assumptions and then the assumption that wins going to take more of your time

principles.text: Launch no-code so you can iterate on marketing pages and experiments fast.
principles.quote: once you launch you have to do marketing and marketing goes around marketing Pages marketing experiments AB tests

principles.text: Run several small bets at once and double down on the best performer after 30 days; don't fall in love with one idea.
principles.quote: never fall in love with the idea for a directory but rather make maybe five bats and then in 30 days look at the one that does the best and then put more time into that

principles.text: After validation, data quality drives growth: experts who see great data share it with their audience.
principles.quote: if that expert who sees your direct sees that the value of the content is high the quality is high they really respect that and they they really want to share with their audience

principles.text: Directories are an easier SEO route than a branded SaaS, and can funnel traffic into your products.
principles.quote: it is much harder to win SEO traffic for a SAS tool than for a directory
